nonblocking_findings: PDF p.223 (printed 215), Arheshet block: the Hebrew line 'אַם שַׁבָּת.[זִכְרוֹן]תְּקִיעָתֵנוּ' prints with no space between the period and the bracket, or between the bracket and the next word. It reads as cramped beside the normal word spacing elsewhere. This is a small spacing issue, not clipping. The English '[the memory of]' brackets print correctly.

PDF p.224→225 (printed 216→217): the last stanza (וּכְמוֹ מַכְנִים בְּזוֹ) has all its Hebrew on p.224, but its English runs onto the top of p.225 ('of the accuser at the breath of the sound of the Shofar.'), leaving the left Hebrew column empty beside it. It is readable and in the right order, but the stanza row is split across pages. Consider keeping each paired row on one page if the stylesheet allows.

PDF p.222 (printed 214): the HE-only rubric lines 'תקיעה: שברים: תקיעה:' and 'קהל וחזן' print across the full width with no English counterpart. The brief says HE-only lines are a deliberate stylesheet choice, so this is noted only to confirm it was seen.
verdict: Approved for pages 222–227 (printed 214–219), covering the end of Zikhronot, the shofar-blowing rubric, Arheshet and the alphabetic Shofar piyyut (stanzas א through ש). There is no clipping or overlap. Hebrew and English are clear and readable, and the running heads and page numbers alternate correctly. Hebrew and English stanzas line up row by row, except for one row that splits across the 224→225 page break. The ↗ source-page markers sit inline and don't collide with any text. No footnotes or notes fall in this range. The priestly-blessing introduction, the ending, the missing-source label and the credits are not in this range, so none were checked.
